pull_request.title: Avoid overflow in saturated PPO surrogate branches
pull_request.body:
PPO exponentiates the log-probability ratio before applying its clipping objective. For a nonnegative advantage, the objective is already bounded above in ratio space, but a finite float32 log ratio can overflow during exponentiation. The resulting backward pass can multiply an infinite exponential by a zero clipping gradient and corrupt the policy parameters. A zero advantage also produces a NaN loss through zero times infinity.

Bound the log ratio by `log1p(clip_param)` before exponentiation only where the advantage is nonnegative. This uses the existing PPO clipping threshold and preserves the clipped objective and its policy gradients. Negative advantages keep their existing ratio path, including meaningful large-ratio penalties.

The regression collects real Gaussian actions, then fits the current means to those actions and changes the standard deviation from 1 to 0.1. With 64 action dimensions the log ratio is finite (184.9753): unchanged source reports the correct saturated loss of -2.4 but produces NaN gradients and parameters. The corrected update remains finite and matches the original formula evaluated in float64. Controls cover zero advantages at both ratio extremes, both clipping branches and the non-saturated negative-advantage objective.

Validation on base `8945bdcbc364f388e14caebf547dbf302d89e491`, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.7.1+cpu and TensorDict 0.7.2:

- Unchanged source: 2 regression failures and 5 passing controls; corrected source: all 7 pass.
- Complete CPU suite: 294 passed, 6 CUDA-only cases skipped, including Gloo and JIT/ONNX tests.
- All configured pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

This change addresses branches whose mathematical policy objective is finite. It does not cap the unbounded negative-advantage objective or claim to prevent every possible overflow.

Validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43674281880
